# Separator font slots and native fallback

Twenty original controls generated by `tools/line_separator_slots_fixture.py`
vary only the U+2028 run's font slots, font hint, East Asian language and
complex-script flag. All ordinary text and paragraph marks use Arial 9pt.
No corpus XML, artwork or standalone font files are included.

The reference application exported the exact source read-only on 2026-09-27.
`tools/record_line_separator_slots.py` records the font used by the PDF text
operator containing U+2028, rather than inferring it from the page's resource
inventory. It also records independent Start/Sample/Tail baselines. The source,
case inventory and PDF are hash-bound by the native-reference test. Regenerating
the source is deterministic; a changed source requires a fresh native reference.

Observed on this installation:

- Default-hint Arial uses MS Gothic regardless of the four tested East Asian
  font declarations. EastAsian language ja-JP, zh-CN, zh-TW or ko-KR alone changes
  neither that font choice nor the three measured baselines.
- EastAsian-hint Arial/Calibri slots use MS Mincho. An explicit MS Gothic slot
  uses MS Gothic. The Times New Roman EastAsian-slot exception returns to the
  Arial ASCII slot and its MS Gothic fallback, consistent with the existing
  MS-OI29500 section 2.1.88 classification rule.
- A Times New Roman high-ANSI slot uses its own separator glyph; Courier New
  uses MS Mincho. Setting the complex-script flag selects the explicitly
  declared Times New Roman complex-script slot in both cases.

These controls support the current slot classifier and isolate a subsequent
glyph-fallback issue. They do not establish a universal OS fallback order,
justify replacing all missing glyphs with a named Japanese font, or certify
the app's separator painting. No production mapping changed.

The source opens as twenty editable app pages. No-edit ZIP preservation,
insertion, unrelated-part retention, exact undo and edited reopening pass with
no browser errors. Source plus three exports pass four XML schema checks. Four
native-reference/slot tests pass. Native/app page-count agreement does not imply
matching glyphs or line metrics. Private browser workflow and schema logs are
under task-workspace `<work>/separator-slots`.

Windows font registration includes MS Gothic but not MS Mincho here. MS Mincho,
Avenir Next LT Pro and Daytona files were located in the reference application's private cloud
font cache. They were not registered, copied into this repository, or loaded
into browser tests. Approval for private local test use was requested under the
user's explicit commercial-resource rule; these controls do not depend on that
approval because they use the already-authorized reference application.
